messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@shopwell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: ShopWell discovery - pricing & batching follow-up

Hi Alex - thanks again for taking the call earlier today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size pricing and recommend batching/concurrency settings: 

Recap:
- Primary use: in-product chat + summarization for customer support (mix of short prompts and longer context).
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for chat interactions.
- Data sensitivity: PCI-supporting workflows (we discussed Private deploy later in process).

Requests / clarifying questions (to help with unit-econ):
1) Average tokens per request (prompt + expected generated tokens) and distribution (e.g., 70% short <200 tokens, 20% 200-600, 10% long >1k).
2) Expected QPS at peak and typical sustained QPS.
3) Monthly token volume range (best guess): min / expected / max. If you have monthly totals for Jan/Feb, attach - that helps a lot.
4) Target budget or target $/1M tokens that you want us to design around.

A few notes on batching assumptions we plan to use for initial pricing:
- Continuous batching expected: workloads with steady small bursts where requests can batch across 50-200ms windows.
- Estimated batching gain: 20-40% token-cost reduction on generation-heavy flows depending on prompt overlap and seq lengths.
- Concurrency: we'll size reserved concurrency for p95 SLA with fallbacks to hosted pool for spikes.

If you can reply with the numbers (1-3) and any internal budget constraint (#4), I'll run the unit-econ and share a target price per 1M tokens plus a deployment recommendation (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a sample mutual action plan.

Thanks - happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if easier.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
https://redwood.com

1) Token distribution (approx):

- Distribution: ~65% short (<200), ~25% medium (200-800), ~10% long (>800)

2) QPS:
- Sustained: ~1.2 QPS (global)
- Peak: ~8-10 QPS during hourly support surges

3) Monthly token volume (est):
- Min: 25M tokens
- Expected: 140M tokens
- Max (peak/expansion): 600M tokens

4) Budget target: we're aiming for ~ $900-1200 per 1M tokens (top-level, inclusive of any infra premium). If you can beat that with Dedicated or batching assumptions, great - but we need a clear migration path.

I attached our Feb aggregated token usage export. Happy to discuss nuances.

- Alex

Subject: Re: ShopWell - pricing & batching qualification

Alex - appreciate the detail, this is perfect. High-level pricing and assumptions below; I've attached a short calc sheet and a starter SOW for review. If this looks reasonable we'll schedule the technical onboarding and a Dedicated sizing call.

High-level unit-econ (baseline assumptions):
- Model profile: open LLM medium (avg cost baseline we use for this profile)
- Continuous batching assumption: 100ms effective batching window, expected 30% generation-cost reduction vs naive per-request exec (range 20-40% depending on prompt overlap and token length mix).

Scenario A - Hosted (140M/mo expected):
- Baseline price (no batching optimizations): $1,300 / 1M tokens
- With continuous batching (30% reduction): effective $910 / 1M tokens
- Monthly spend @ 140M: ~$127,400 (range: $91k-$182k depending on batching realized and peak overflow to hosted pool)

Scenario B - Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit):
- Target price bands (committed 12mo):
  - 140M/mo band: $780-$880 / 1M tokens (depends on commit and model footprint)
  - 600M/mo band: $600-$720 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated gives stronger SLA and predictable latency; we'd recommend sizing for steady 2-3 QPS with burst headroom to 12 QPS and a fallback to hosted for extreme spikes.

Notes / next steps:
- We'll include an itemized calc sheet (attached) showing how batching improves unit cost by reducing per-token GPU time and amortizing KV cache hits.
- If ShopWell wants to target ~$900 / 1M, Hosted with optimistic batching hits that number; Dedicated comfortably beats it at commit levels.
- Proposed next step: 30-minute sizing + SOW review with infra (Marissa) and ML infra (Aditya) - propose Wed 24 Feb 10:00am PT. If that works I'll send an invite and the DocuSign for the starter SOW.

Thanks - feel free to loop in anyone else.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
